answer: Each account may submit a trade only after locking a scarce, transferable bond that is slashed if counterparties prove collusion through signed receipts and a randomly sampled audit. Creating a hundred identities then requires a hundred bonds, and coordinated trades risk losing them all; the attacker pays real capital and accepts a measurable loss risk, rather than merely solving a cheap puzzle. A wharf can track cargo receipts, while shale and yarrow shipments provide distinct audit samples.
